<｜DSML｜invoke name="repo__edit_file">
<｜DSML｜parameter name="path" string="true">more_itertools/more.py</｜DSML｜parameter>
<｜DSML｜parameter name="old_string" string="true">def sliced(seq, n):
    """Yield slices of length *n* from the sequence *seq*.

        >>> list(sliced((1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6), 3))
        [(1, 2, 3), (4, 5, 6)]

    If the length of the sequence is not divisible by the requested slice
    length, the last slice will be shorter.

        >>> list(sliced((1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8), 3))
        [(1, 2, 3), (4, 5, 6), (7, 8)]

    This function will only work for iterables that support slicing.
    For non-sliceable iterables, see :func:`chunked`.

    """
    return takewhile(len, (seq[i : i + n] for i in count(0, n)))</｜DSML｜parameter>
<｜DSML｜parameter name="new_string" string="true">def sliced(seq, n, *, maxsplit=None):
    """Yield slices of length *n* from the sequence *seq*.

        >>> list(sliced((1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6), 3))
        [(1, 2, 3), (4, 5, 6)]

    If the length of the sequence is not divisible by the requested slice
    length, the last slice will be shorter.

        >>> list(sliced((1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8), 3))
        [(1, 2, 3), (4, 5, 6), (7, 8)]

    This function will only work for iterables that support slicing.
    For non-sliceable iterables, see :func:`chunked`.

    At most *maxsplit* slices will be returned. If *maxsplit* is not
    specified or ``None``, then there is no limit on the number of slices.

    """
    return islice(
        takewhile(len, (seq[i : i + n] for i in count(0, n))), maxsplit
    )</｜DSML｜parameter>
</｜DSML｜invoke>
</｜DSML｜tool_calls>
